# Instructions for accurately documenting excessive industrial emissions in an air-quality report

1. Start with the monitoring records.

completion:
Use on-site measurements and data from continuous emission monitoring systems (CEMS).
3. Utilize air quality monitoring stations nearby, if available.
4. Analyze the dispersion modeling data.
5. Document the types and concentrations of pollutants.
6. Detail the duration and frequency of excessive emissions.
7. Record meteorological data to understand dispersion.
8. Compare measurements with regulatory standards and permits.
9. Document any patterns or recurring issues related to excessive emissions.
10. Include digital photos or videos of emission releases.
11. Note dates, times, durations, and any associated weather conditions.
12. Reference any control measures or mitigation strategies lacking or not being used.
13. Include assessments of potential health and environmental impacts.
14. Summarize the volume and flow rates involved in the emissions.
15. Provide data on the affected areas and populations.
